## My Thinking

I've farmed this land my whole life. My father grew wheat and corn on this same ground in Quzhou, and I do the same. At 70, I don't have the strength I used to, but the rotation hasn't changed — winter wheat goes in after harvest, corn goes in after the wheat comes out in June. That's what the land here does. That's what my neighbors do. I'm not going to try something new at my age.

I have about 5 mu. It's the same 5 mu every year, wheat first then corn on the same ground.

For seeds, I go to Old Chen's shop in the village. I'll get the same improved wheat variety I've used the last few years — I don't remember the name, just the bag — and the hybrid corn seed he recommends. Last year's corn was decent. I'll do the same.

Fertilizer: I put down compound fertilizer when I plant, then urea top-dress later. I don't weigh it out — I go by what looks right pouring it, same as my father did. The wheat needs water four times: before the ground freezes, at jointing, at heading, once more at grain fill. I pump from the well for all of it. Corn is in the rainy months so maybe twice.

My son comes back to help with tillage. We use the rotary tiller both times. Ploughing deep is too much work now. I spray herbicide on the wheat in winter and once before heading for the rust. Corn just gets one spray after it emerges.

I don't expect big yields. 450 jin per mu for wheat, maybe 550 for corn. Enough to sell a little, keep some, and get through another year.
